newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Australia recall Warne but drop Slater.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Australia recall Warne but drop Slater.

text.p: Australia on Monday recalled leg-spinner Shane Warne after injury but discarded opener Michael Slater for the first cricket test against the West Indies.
Warne, who missed the recent tours of Sri Lanka and India because of finger surgery, was named in a 12-man squad for the test in Brisbane, starting on Friday.
Australia also left out spinners Brad Hogg and Peter McIntyre from the side that lost the one-off test against India in New Delhi last month by seven wickets.
Slater has been replaced by fellow opener Matthew Elliot, who forced his way into the test side with a century for an Australian XI against West Indies on Saturday.
Selectors announced the squad on Monday at Hobart's Bellerive Oval during the fourth and final day of a tour match regarded as a selection trial for Australia's fringe test candidates.
Warne returned to first-class cricket as Victoria captain 10 days ago but has bowled only sparingly by his own standards in two domestic Shefffield Shield matches.
He underwent surgery in May to repair ligaments in the ring finger of his bowling hand and has since been troubled by swelling of the joint after exercise.
Warne said he would hold nothing back during the first test even if doing so caused him to aggravate the injury.
"It's full-on now -- if I break down halfway through the first Test, so be it," he said.
"I'm ready to bowl as much as (Australia captain) Mark Taylor wants me to bowl -- if he wants me to bowl 50 overs, I'm ready to bowl 50 overs for him," Warne said.
His return strengthens Australia's bowling attack after injuries ruled out veteran fast bowler Craig McDermott and fellow paceman Damien Fleming.
New ball strike bowler Glenn McGrath was named in the test line-up but he faces a fitness test on a blistered heel on Wednesday.
Fast bowlers Michael Kasprowicz and Jason Gillespie are expected to challenge for the remaining berth in the pace attack alongside McGrath and Paul Reiffel.
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Ricky Ponting, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Glenn McGrath, Michael Kasprowicz, Jason Gillespie.
